To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
68Ga‐PSA PET/CT has a high sensitivity and specificity in detecting prostate cancer in men with negative or equivocal mpMRI, and can be used as a primary diagnostic tool.
68Ga‐PSM PET/CT may be a promising imaging modality for primary diagnosis of prostate cancer in patients in whom conventional imaging modalities have failed to identify a prostate lesion.

68Ga‐PSA PET/CT is highly sensitive and specific in men with negative MRI and/or contraindications for MRI, and may represent the most appropriate imaging tool for the diagnosis of clinically relevant prostate cancer in these men.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
68Ga‐PSA‐11 PET/CT may represent the most accurate imaging technique for the detection of prostate cancer, especially in patients with negative MRI.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
68Ga labeled PSMA-positron emission tomography/CT may be used as a primary diagnostic modality for prostate cancer in a select group.
68Ga labeled PSMA PET/CT is an excellent tool for primary prostate cancer detection and can be used as a primary tool in patients with contrindications to or negative mpMRI.
68Ga labeled PSMA PET/CT is a useful tool to detect and localize prostate cancer, even if the multiparametric MRI is negative or equivocal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 68Ga labeled PSMA PET/CT is a very useful imaging technique for the detection of primary prostate cancer in patients in whom mpMRI is not possible or is negative and who are candidates for a repeat prostate biopsy.

the use of 2 different parameters (maximum standardized uptake value and maximum‐to‐ background standardized uptake value ratio), which are easily available on 68Ga‐PSA PET/CT, can be used to discriminate clinically significant from non‐clinically significant disease.
68Ga labeled PSMA PET/CT can be used for primary detection of PC in patients with persistently high PSA and negative DRE and at least 2 negative biopsy results.
